analysis.title: GS McGeoch - GS Materials Nov 5...MT inline (recovery trade), LUN solid (cuts prodn on weather), Minerrs v Banks Downunder, Coppers labour risk, Utilities results a plenty
key_insights: Desk sees China buying gold and selling copper as the busier trade than the prior day, which the author describes as an AI trade for Chinese participants rather than a stock-out trade. Gold open interest is flat, with shorts covering and longs adding on low volume.
Copper is quiet except for physical premiums, which are back at all-time highs (CECN0002 Index). The desk reads this as where physical tightness is showing up.
Desk positioning read: macro positioning is very close to zero across the franchise. Faster CTAs are short or flat, medium-term players are long but not extended, and China specs had gone short.

On gold, the author says positioning, the oil price and the move in rates each justify the move, and they can be compounded if the direction of travel in all three is sustained. The author still sees a lot of hesitation.

Copper supply is the support. Cochilco took 470kt out of its guide last week, and a GS note says Chile labour negotiations add another supply risk into 2027. A China analyst said the scrap tax rebate bottleneck only changes on a high and fast price move.

ASX miners rose 7% (GSXAAUMI Index) while NAB.AU fell 5.5% on its result (asset quality deterioration, cost growth, negative organic capital generation). The author notes the UK lacks Australia's resource backbone.
FMG is issuing a US bond amid continued friction with Chinese buyers. The stock is +9% and the author stays short.

Steel: the US curve is most likely to roll up at the front. The 3-month contract is up $50/st this week and the front is up $100/st in the last month, on tight supply and mills not offering spot ahead of Cal27 contract pricing. The author says it feels like the back end of the move. EUR steel is going sideways, with about $750 at the front in contango.

MT.NA: Q3 was as expected with a small beat, no real change to outlook, and the stock is +6% (+4% vs SXPP), above the author's +1-2% estimate because of sponsorship. Q3 EBITDA was $2.02bn vs company-compiled $1.97bn. Cash flow was -$440m vs consensus -$90m on a -$490m working capital build. Net debt was $10.4bn vs consensus $10.03bn. The open question is recovery to 2027 consensus EBITDA of $10.7bn.

LUN.CN: adjusted EBITDA $648m, +5% vs consensus. Production guidance was cut a further 15kt (25kt total) on Chile weather. Unit costs were unchanged (Q3 $2.01, -11% vs GS), and capex was trimmed. The stock starts 1-2% lower vs SXPP. The author still sees copper as upside asymmetry on stock-out risk and sees a question mark over ANTO from the weather impact.

Gold Fields: stock +11% in a SA market that was bid (IMP +15%, ANG +12.5%) after SA closed the previous day. Q3 was softer, with attributable production of 621k oz (-5% vs consensus). FY guide is unchanged but needs a strong Q4. GS initiated at neutral on delivery and Tarkwa uncertainty, with under 6 months remaining on the leases and no timetable for a government response.

Tenaris: stock +5%. 4Q EBITDA was $756m, a 17% beat. Tubes EBITDA/t was $775/t. FCF ex working capital was $538m, and net cash rose to $3.8bn. The 4Q guide is at least in line with 3Q, which implies more than 4% FY26 upgrades. The desk calls this conservative and likes the Americas and Middle East mix.

Utilities: the desk is long ENGI vs VIE. ENGI +2% on better energy management and renewables, with new guidance pointing to 4% upgrades. VIE -1% on in-line results. EDP +1% on CEO departure. EDPR beat on headline but underlying was a miss. Orsted +2% with EBITDA 4% ahead. NG +1% with EPS 4% ahead. Nordex Q3 EBITDA was a 15% beat, with new margin guidance implying a 12% consensus EBITDA upgrade.

FCX approved the $4.5bn Bagdad expansion (previously $3.5bn in 2023). Output goes to 400mlbs copper from 175m and moly to 20m lbs from 8m, with first production in mid 2030. Capital intensity is about $45k/t (about $35k/t with moly credit), with project break-even at $4/lb copper and $20/lb moly. GS compares this with AAL's $11k/t brownfield figure.

Read-across to RIO/BHP: Resolution is estimated at $12-13bn for 500kt, which the author thinks looks conservative against the FCX capex. A possible S232 action could speed up a US project with a downstream investment commitment. The author would see any Resolution update as a negative catalyst.

Chile labour exposure by company: BHP about 75% of copper production (Escondida, Spence), RIO about 35% (Escondida), LUN about 40% (Caserones), ANTO about 55% (Los Pelambres) and about 30% (Centinela). GLEN and AAL have more limited exposure.
CIA: after results GS sees a risk the company may need equity funding if margins and cash flow do not improve materially. The stock trades at about 0.4x GS NAV of about A$4.1/sh.

China midday wrap: SHCOMP opened 1% lower and recovered, with resistance at the 20DMA (3,701). STAR 50 is up over 2.5% and ChiNext up 1.3%. Turnover is projected above RMB 2.5tn, the highest since early August and +50% vs the 20-day average. Renewables lead on policy support, and oil and coal fell with crude.

market_movers.rationale: MT (ArcelorMittal) Q3 EBITDA of $2.02bn beat the company-compiled $1.97bn. Net debt and cash flow were weaker than consensus, and the stock is up 6% on sponsorship as a recovery trade.
Tenaris 4Q EBITDA beat by 17% and the 4Q guide implies more than 4% FY26 upgrades. The desk likes the Americas and Middle East mix.
Desk is long ENGI vs VIE. ENGI results were driven by better energy management and renewables, and new guidance points to 4% upgrades.
Gold Fields initiated at neutral on the need to see delivery step up and Tarkwa lease uncertainty. Q3 production of 621k oz was 5% below consensus.
FMG is short on the desk's view given the US bond issuance and continued friction with Chinese buyers, although the stock rose 9%.
CIA may need equity funding if margins and cash flow do not improve, and the stock trades at about 0.4x GS NAV of about A$4.1/sh.
Bagdad expansion approval at $4.5bn reads as in line with the Q3 update. Volumes go to 400mlbs copper, and first production is mid 2030.
LUN adjusted EBITDA beat consensus by 5% despite a further 15kt production cut on Chile weather. Costs were controlled and capex was trimmed.

sector_views.rationale: Desk sees copper as upside asymmetry on stock-out risk, with supply tight from Chile weather, labour risk and the scrap tax rebate bottleneck.
Results were mixed across the group. The desk prefers ENGI over VIE and sees EDP's CEO change as interesting but at risk of a fade.
NAB.AU fell 5.5% on asset quality deterioration, cost growth and negative organic capital generation, while miners rose 7%.

earnings_insights: MT.NA Q3 (reported 11/5): EBITDA $2.02bn vs company-compiled consensus $1.97bn. Cash flow -$440m vs consensus -$90m on a -$490m working capital build. Net debt $10.4bn vs consensus $10.03bn. 2027 consensus EBITDA is $10.7bn.
LUN.CN Q3 (reported 11/5): adjusted EBITDA $648m, +5% vs consensus. Production guide cut a further 15kt for weather, 25kt in total. Q3 unit cost $2.01, -11% vs GS.
Gold Fields Q3 (reported): attributable production 621k oz, -5% vs consensus. FY guide unchanged and needs a strong Q4.

Tenaris 4Q (reported): EBITDA $756m, a 17% beat. Tubes EBITDA/t $775/t. FCF ex working capital $538m. Net cash $3.8bn. The 4Q guide is at least in line with 3Q, which implies more than 4% FY26 upgrades.
ENGI (reported 11/5): results beat on better energy management and renewables, with new guidance pointing to 4% upgrades. VIE: in-line results, guidance reiterated.

EDPR (reported 11/5): headline numbers beat but were driven by lower tax and rotation, and the desk calls underlying a miss. Orsted: EBITDA 4% beat. NG: EPS 4% ahead of consensus, net debt £48.8bn vs consensus £50bn.
Nordex Q3 (reported): EBITDA a 15% beat vs company-compiled consensus. New margin guidance at the midpoint of revenue guidance (€8.2-€9.0bn) implies a 12% company-compiled consensus EBITDA upgrade.
NAB.AU (reported 11/5): the stock fell 5.5% on asset quality deterioration, cost growth and negative organic capital generation.
CIA (post results): GS sees a risk of equity funding, with the stock at about 0.4x revised NAV of about A$4.1/sh.

trade_ideas.description: Long ENGI vs short VIE (pair trade)
trade_ideas.rationale: ENGI delivered a strong result on better energy management and renewables, with guidance pointing to 4% upgrades, while VIE was in line.
FMG is issuing a US bond amid friction with Chinese buyers, and the author says it looks messy.
trade_ideas.risk: The stock rose 9% on the day.

risk_factors: Chile copper labour negotiations at Escondida, Spence, Caserones and Los Pelambres add supply risk into 2027.
Weather in Chile has cut production guidance at LUN and creates a question mark over ANTO.
Copper price could rise sharply if the scrap tax rebate bottleneck stays in place, which hurts shorts.
Gold Fields faces Tarkwa lease uncertainty, with under 6 months remaining on the leases.
CIA may need equity funding if margins and cash flow do not improve.
EDP's CEO change could fade after the initial reaction.
vol_and_positioning: Gold open interest is flat, with shorts covering and longs adding on low volume.
Macro positioning is very close to zero across the desk's franchise. Faster CTAs are short or flat, and medium-term players are long but not extended.
China specs had gone short copper, per price action.
The market is not long copper and not short, per price action.
geopolitical: FMG is issuing a US bond amid continued friction with Chinese counterparties.
A possible S232 action could speed up a US copper project with a downstream investment commitment. The author says this is feedback only, with no guide.
Ghana's government is not engaging on Gold Fields' Tarkwa lease and has said there is no timetable for a response.
China domestic policy support is driving renewables, and the A-H discount is narrowing with A-share buybacks.

tension_points.bull_case: Supply is tight, with the Cochilco guide cut, Chile weather and labour risk, and physical premiums at all-time highs. The author sees upside asymmetry on stock-out risk.
tension_points.bear_case: Demand is weak, and the market is not long copper. Chinese specs had gone short on price action.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A high and fast price move would release supply tension by changing the China scrap tax rebate bottleneck, which would hurt shorts rather than invalidate the bull case.

theme_stances.key_argument: The supply side is the support for copper even with weak demand.
theme_stances.evidence: In Copper the supply side is your crutch

theme_stances.key_argument: ENGI delivered stronger results and upgrades than VIE.
